== Biography ==
William Glasgow was born in 1701 in Stevenston, Ayrshire, Scotland, and was christened the same year. His parents were John Glasgow and Agnas Spark. According to Elaine Comes on Wikitree, William had a brother named Hugh who married Janet Kilpatrick. They were sons of John Glasgow and Agnes Spark. Agnes Glasgow’s father was William Glasgow, and her mother was Margaret Montfodd/Montfort.

William’s daughter, Agnes Glasgow, had three sisters: Grizell, Katherine, and Margaret Glasgow.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1057]] is assessed at 99% (proved). The retained Stevenston baptism citation names William’s father John Glasgow and mother Agnas Spark. John-1057 represents that same John/Agnes parental household, also found in George’s 1687 Kilwinning entry. The specific couple identifies the record father strongly.

Recorded William and Spark household; the 1700/1701 date discrepancy and John’s own Edinburgh childhood remain separate.

Next useful test: Resolve the event-date discrepancy from the original register without reopening the named parents.

Source basis already held: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYZK-3JZ “Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950”, a database available on FamilySearch, where you can find William Glasgow’s christening record [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYZK-3JZ].]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.


=== Possible Irvine–Dundonald identity and ancestry ===

Prefer the Irvine father account William [[Glasgow-1055]] as the same adult as the Dundonald weaver William [[Glasgow-3586]], at 56% subjective identity confidence. The Irvine entries name Wm or William as father of Grizell in 1724, Agnes in 1725, Katherine in 1727 and Margaret in 1729. The Dundonald entry names William Glasgow, weaver at Achenyeards, as Jean’s father on 1 October 1732. An existing adult household in the adjoining Irvine parish followed by the 1732 Dundonald household is a specific chronological and local fit, and is preferred to matching an otherwise untraced childhood profile alone. This is an inferred adult identity: the Irvine transcripts do not state the father’s trade or Achenyeards residence.

Select John [[Glasgow-1057]] as the Dundonald William’s possible working father at 46%. This is an assessment of the complete father proposition, including both the 56% adult identity and the further identification of the Irvine adult with the Stevenston child cited as born or baptised on 30 November 1700 to John Glasgow and Agnas Spark (OPR615,10/3,frame11). The current William-1055 account estimates 1701; the citation and estimate are not silently harmonised. John-1057 is the existing account for that named parent. Its separate identification with an Edinburgh child baptised in1661, and its own earlier ancestry, retain their existing qualifications. The percentages are individual judgments, not measured frequencies or independent values to multiply.

No record names the Dundonald father’s own parents, connects the two adult households, or supplies an occupation for the Irvine father. William [[Glasgow-3288]], baptised at Kilbirnie on20August1704, remains a compatible alternative. William [[Glasgow-1061]], whose maintained transcript gives birth25June1715 and baptism26June1715 at Byres,Kilwinning, could have been a father at seventeen in1732; this is a weaker generation fit, not an exclusion. An unrepresented William remains possible. No wife’s death, remarriage, exact migration or craft inheritance is invented. Katherine’s1727 transcript names Mary Monfodd, while the other three Irvine entries name Margaret with Monfood/Montford/Montfod variants; this maternal distinction remains unresolved. The undated Mary Montfort marriage attached to William-1061 cannot identify the1727 mother merely by her name. No maternity is transferred from either William account.

The two William profiles remain separate accounts, with no merge and no claim of two proved William sons. Jean’s existing father link stays ungraded. The1733 child’s selected father remains possible52%, and Barbara Stevenson’s maternity remains99%; neither is strengthened by this upstream hypothesis. Jean’s mother remains unknown. Barbara’s existing pairing with the Dundonald father is ungraded and does not establish a remarriage after the Irvine household. Preserve all vital fields and previously selected relatives. Resolve the possible duplicate before a live attachment or merger. This is one new possible father proposal based on reassessment of held transcripts and profile citations; no original parish register was newly inspected and no live edit is made.

James Richmond’s Irvine account in the Old Statistical Account,volume7,printedpp169–170 (PDFpages1–2), describes the part of the settlement south of the river as belonging to Dundonald parish. The inspected printed page supports close geographical context, not this man’s residence in that part of Irvine or an individual migration in1732.

Inspect the original Irvine1724–1729 and Dundonald1732–1733 entries for the father’s occupation, residence and witnesses, and compare the Stevenston1700 entry with the adult’s later household. Seek a marriage, tenancy or kirk-session record distinguishing the Irvine father from William-3288 and William-1061. Test Mary versus Margaret independently; do not create a wife’s death to explain a later pairing.<ref name="IrvineDundonald2026">[https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3573951&tab=this Grizell Glasgow, 09 Aug 1724, Irvine; held Findmypast transcript]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3574073&tab=this Agnes Glasgow, 07 Dec 1725, Irvine; held Findmypast transcript]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3574234&tab=this Katherine Glasgow, 03 Sep 1727, Irvine; held Findmypast transcript]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3574367&tab=this Margaret Glasgow, 05 Jan 1729, Irvine; held Findmypast transcript]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3536699&tab=this Jean Glasgow, 01 Oct 1732, Dundonald; held Findmypast transcript]; [https://stataccscot.ed.ac.uk/data/pdfs/account1/StAS.1.7.169.P.Ayrshire.Irvine.pdf#page=2 James Richmond, Old Statistical Account, Irvine,vol7,p170 / PDFpage2; geography only]. Held parish transcripts and profile citations reassessed; original parish images uninspected. Printed geography context only.</ref>

The1727 transcript gives the mother as Mary Monfodd, while the1724,1725 and1729 entries give Margaret. The difference is unresolved. The linked [[Glasgow-812]] page concerns a different,nineteenth-century woman and does not support this family. The quoted Stevenston date30November1700 and approximate1701 birth require comparison with the original entry.
